inlines.v: CONTEMN, verb transitive [Latin , to despise; to drive away.] 1. To despise; to consider and treat as mean and despicable; to scorn. In whose eyes a vile person is contemned. Psalms 15:4. 2. To slight; to neglect as unworthy of regard; to reject with disdain. Wherefore do the wicked contemn God. Psalms 10:13. They contemn the counsel of the Most High. Psalms 107:11.
